history.period: 19th century (shrine); 1911 CE construction per some sources; major expansion in the 20th century
history.summary: POSSIBLE DUPLICATE: seq 296 in this dataset ('Shri Khodiyar Mata Temple', file 296.json, id 'khodiyar-mata-temple-rajpara') is the same temple - one of the two records should be merged or removed. TOWN CORRECTION: CSV lists the town as Bhavnagar, but the temple is at Rajpara village (Shihor/Sihor taluka, Bhavnagar district), about 15-16 km from Bhavnagar city on the Bhavnagar-Rajkot highway, on the banks of the Tataniya/Tataliya lake. The temple is dedicated to Khodiyar Mata, a warrior goddess born in the Charan caste around 700 CE (per tradition), revered as the ancestral (kuldevi) and guiding goddess of the Gohils and the Bhavnagar royal family. Legend: Maharaja Wakhatsinhji Gohil (who ruled Bhavnagar 1748-1816 per sources) prayed for the goddess to come to his capital Sihor; she agreed on condition he not look back, but he turned at Rajpara, and she settled there. CONFLICT (verify): sources disagree on construction history - trawell.in says the temple was constructed in 1911 CE by the then Maharaja of Bhavnagar, while yatradham/blog and gujaratdarshanguide describe a small shrine founded by Wakhatsinhji later grandly expanded by Maharaja Krishnakumarsinhji (who also built the road, drinking-water facilities and the Khodiyar Mandir railway station on the Bhavnagar-Dhola line, and founded the Shri Khodiyar Mandir Trust in 1953). A mountain-top shrine behind the temple is linked by a ropeway. Lapsi (broken-wheat sweet) is the main prasad, and free meals are served to visitors. Coordinates from datagemba's temple-specific listing; marked approximate within the Rajpara shrine complex.

name: Shree Khodiyar Mata Mandir, Bhavnagar
town_description: Rajpara is a village in Sihor taluka of Bhavnagar district, Gujarat, on the Bhavnagar-Rajkot highway about 15-16 km from Bhavnagar city. It is famous for the Rajpara Khodiyar Mata temple, one of the oldest and largest Khodiyar shrines in Saurashtra, set beside the Tataniya lake. The village also has its own railway halt, Khodiyar Mandir, on the Bhavnagar-Dhola line.

travel.airport: Bhavnagar Airport, approx. 20-25 km by road (verify).
travel.railway: Khodiyar Mandir halt on the Bhavnagar-Dhola line serves the temple; Bhavnagar Terminus is approx. 15-16 km (verify).
travel.road: On the Bhavnagar-Rajkot highway, approx. 15-16 km from Bhavnagar; state buses, taxis and private vehicles; the trust provides pilgrim facilities including dharamshalas.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Sundays, Tuesdays and full-moon days (Poonam) are the busiest and most devotional times.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Reported approx. 5:00 AM to 10:00 PM daily, with morning aarti around 5:00-5:30 AM and evening aarti around 7:00 PM (verify - sources differ on exact aarti times). Free meals (lunch/dinner) are served to visitors (verify current practice). The temple trust runs dharamshalas for overnight stays.
